title: Neural Network–Based Real-Time Wind Energy Estimation
content: This work proposes a real-time estimation approach for the power produced by a direct current wind power system, based on an artificial neural network (ANN). The latter uses the Levenberg–Marquardt training algorithm. The model is trained using experimental data from a LabVolt wind test bench and can predict instantaneous power from measured operating variables, taking into account load variations and simulated wind conditions. The methodology includes the collection of experimental data, training of the neural network, and validation of the model under different operating conditions. The ANN model demonstrated excellent predictive performance. For current prediction, the MSE, RMSE, MAE, and R² values were 2.8271e−5, 0.0053, 0.0031, and 1.0000, respectively. For power forecasting, the corresponding values were 0.16245, 0.4030, 0.1885, and 1.0000, respectively, indicating near-perfect agreement between the forecast data and the measured data.
